title: The Lion and the Mouse
author: Aesop (retold)
summary: 小さなネズミが、網にかかった大きなライオンを助けます。イソップの有名な寓話。

source.note: Retold in simple English from Aesop’s Fables (public domain).

paragraphs: A big lion is sleeping under a tree. A little mouse runs over his face. The lion wakes up. He is angry. He puts his big paw on the mouse.
“Please don’t eat me!” says the mouse. “Let me go. One day, I can help you.”
The lion laughs. “You? Help me? You are so small!” But he is not hungry, and the mouse is funny. So he lets the mouse go.
A few days later, some hunters come to the forest. They want to catch the lion. They put a big net on the ground. The lion walks into the net. He cannot get out. He roars and roars.
The little mouse hears the lion. She runs to him. She sees the net. “Don’t worry,” she says. “I can help.”
The mouse has small, sharp teeth. She bites the net. She bites and bites. Soon there is a big hole in the net. The lion walks out. He is free!
“Thank you, little mouse,” says the lion. “You were right. A small friend can be a great friend.”
